question: How does a Core Advancement Proposal (CAP) move from idea to activated protocol change on Stellar?

golden.answer: A CAP starts as public discussion and a Draft markdown PR in stellar-protocol/core, moves to Awaiting Decision, then a Final Comment Period leads to Accepted or rejection (or back to Draft). Accepted means the specification is approved; Implemented and Final follow. None of these is network activation, which happens when validators agree to a scheduled upgrade through SCP quorum sets, not a node-count majority or XLM-holder vote. SEPs set ecosystem conventions and do not change consensus rules.
keyFacts: CAP path: Draft, Awaiting Decision, FCP, Accepted, Implemented, Final.
CAP status is separate from implementation, release and network activation.
Activation is validator agreement through quorum sets, not a token or majority vote.
CAPs change protocol; SEPs are ecosystem interoperability standards.
avoid: Do NOT list Implementation Review as a current status or equate Accepted or Final with activation.
golden.notes: core/README describes Final as accepted by a majority of validators; an answer quoting that as the registry definition is not wrong.

Grader note 2026-11-02: stellar-protocol core/README.md defines Final as a CAP 'accepted by a majority of validators (nodes) on the network'. An answer that attributes that wording to the registry as the definition of the Final label does not fire avoid[2]. avoid[2] fires only when the answer says SCP network activation itself is decided by a global node-count majority or a token-holder vote.
